B introduces the wrong Upload API and extensive explicitly forbidden association and retry machinery.","reasons":["A adds the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). B instead accepts ...FilesUploadOption, breaking the specified API and existing FilesOption usage.","A reuses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\" and preserves the supplied filename and content. Its retry test verifies the multipart metadata and payload on both attempts.","A keeps scope focused and does not add association fields or refactor the shared retry transport. B adds seven association options and multipart-field machinery despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields.","B modifies Raw.Do and changes ownership/retry semantics for all seekable request bodies, contrary to the instruction not to refactor unrelated retry machinery or change Update behavior indirectly through shared transport code."],"risks_a":["Upload calls the new private add method rather than routing through the existing public Add method, violating the required reuse path.","Add now eagerly buffers every custom body, changing its established lower-level streaming behavior despite the requirement to preserve its behavior.","The visible tests do not directly cover Upload validation or source-reader error propagation, both explicitly requested."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong option type and therefore does not implement the exact required convenience API.","Upload duplicates Add's request construction, response decoding, and error handling instead of routing through Add.","Adds explicitly forbidden association fields and a new parallel option system, increasing API surface and maintenance burden while changing FilesOption behavior expectations for Upload callers such as WithFilesQuery options not being accepted by its signature/type system generally—they use FilesUploadOption only, while contract requires FilesOption behavior unchanged and all FilesOption options accepted syntactically. Note WithFilesRequestOptions happens to implement both, but WithFilesQuery does not, violating exact opts contract." ]}
